svg.text: BAES-CLOUD-HOME
A home that mostly runs itself
one free, open-source brain · any brand · cheap DIY parts · repurposed tech · no ecosystem lock-in
THE BRAIN
Home Assistant
free & open-source software
on a ~$100 Raspberry Pi
in my home, not a
company’s cloud
DIY for a few dollars
ESP32 boards ~$5–10 · mmWave radar ~$15
tracks up to 9 people, each to the spot,
even when they’re sitting perfectly still,
then lights, music & more adapt to who’s
where, the time, the temperature, when
they got home and what others are doing
(TV on? music playing?) · free ESPHome
Hand-me-downs & e-waste
unused & underused tech lying around,
even things I’d once have called broken,
each repurposed for one useful job:
old Raspberry Pi 400 → wall calendar
…that doubles as the spare brain
old laptop → the Zigbee & MQTT hub
2013 mini-PC → firmware & party lights
Speaks every “language”
Zigbee · Matter/Thread · Wi-Fi · Bluetooth
infrared · Ethernet · and, with me:
voice, gesture, distance and text
local control first; the cloud only where
a brand gives no other choice
Big brands, side by side
IKEA · Philips Hue · Sonos · Samsung
Google · Roborock · SwitchBot · WiZ
Tuya / Smart Life · Govee · Clipsal
Sensibo · and plenty more
+ almost anything that isn’t smart
can be hooked in cheaply too
a dozen apps → one home that cooperates
It just knows
Like Santa, it knows when I’m sleeping
and it knows when I’m awake.
It’s tuned to what I want by where I am,
the day, the time and what I’m doing:
lights, music, alarms and the door lock
just happen. Alerts find me on
whatever screen is nearby.
Private & resilient
runs at home; most of it works offline
a backup clone of the brain stands by,
ready to take over in about 5 minutes
daily backups to my NAS and the cloud
no subscriptions required
One remote for the whole home
A custom app I designed from the ground up, running on an affordable Android remote (Astrion HA100).
Touch screen, physical buttons or voice (“hey Pikachu”): TV, music, lights, scenes and alerts in one hand.
Plus two round knob screens I built, one a B&O Essence-style music knob (BæoRemote).
Swap any brand in or out — the brain, the automations and the way I live with it stay the same.
